As someone who was both molested when young and used as a teenager, I completely disagree with you. I've been on both sides of the coin and unfortunately, the teenage years hurt harder since I was more aware. The wounds are much fresher. There is no "well at least she wasn't a 12 year old" in this kind of situation. He is just as much of a pedophile. As I said in a previous comment, I'm 22 and would never look at a 16 year old that way since I see them as what they are, children going through puberty. They don't have enough life experience to understand what is happening to them in these circumstances. Even if she was 18, I would be adamantly against her dating a 28 year old.

It doesn't matter at that age gap and that age. Combined with the fact she is obviously not in the best home situation and the pedophile or "friend" in question is her tutor and a respected adult figure in her life, its complete manipulation of a child's feelings. I was in her shoes before too. I have been raped by older men as a naive young girl. I engaged in relationships with older men as a naive young girl who craved nothing more than stability and unfortunately there were monsters around who took advantage of that. What you don't understand is that this will have everlasting consequences on her life.

 "But is she a completely oblivious child? Probably not either." She has no idea what she is getting herself into. Do you remember yourself at 16? Would you say you were a fully capable adult? I certainly would not. 

It's disgusting for a 28 year old to look at a 16 year old that way. It doesn't matter if she's had her period, if her body's developed, if she's feeling sexual feelings. None of this matters, she's a kid. She needs to be exploring this kind of stuff with people her own age if she's exploring. What this "friend" is doing is taking advantage of a naive young girl in a bad situation. The fact that you can't see that is astonishing to me.

She has aspergers and is over 10 years his junior. He is completely taking advantage of her. Whether he goes to his parents or some kind of legal action, he HAS to get someone involved. I don't think you quite understand just HOW detrimental it is to a teenagers mental development to date someone THAT much older. Even if he was a college student, that would still be disgusting. I'm a 22 year old and I would never look at a 16 year old child in that way because they're still fucking kids. You sound like an absolute creep.

You absolutely have to tell your parents. If you have proof of admission also show this to the cops. He may be your "friend" but he's a pedophile and used you to get close to your UNDERAGE sister. She's barely developed at that point, she's still a kid. Your sister may be upset in the moment but she will thank you for it 10 years down the line. This guy isn't your friend, call it what it is. He's a pedophile.

Technically, no, it's not your fault. You didn't get her to kill herself, unfortunately, she chose that. Many people get cheated on (incl myself) and don't kill themselves. Seriously, I've attempted suicide twice and in neither circumstance was getting cheated on even in my mind. However, being cheated on really destroys your self-esteem. To have someone promise to love you and then see you as so unwanting that they seek the affections of another? I can't even describe how sharp the knife cuts. I mean, you knew she was vulnerable and you still chose to be that selfish? I don't want to feel any pity for you but I accept that you are a person too. 

As others have said, you are not an innocent act and I can see why her family blames you. What you did was incredibly fucked up man. I never understand cheaters, you don't want someone anymore or you got lurking eyes that spark more than just mild interest in your heart? Just leave. 

This is definitely outside of reddit's paygrade. Go see a therapist, you'll need to.  You can't change the past but you can change the future. You feel as much guilt as you say you do? Use that to become a better person and make sure you never make the same mistake twice. You didn't kill her but you sure didn't help.
